news.headline: Wombats Turn Out to Be Great for the Land
news.body: Scientists in South Australia studied the southern hairy-nosed wombat for three years. Its digging helps loosen soil so water can soak in, and it helps spread helpful fungi that plants need to grow. Plants grew thicker where wombats lived, so the researcher says these diggers deserve protection.

news.headline: 14-Year-Old Uses an Underwater Robot to Study Kelp
news.body: Linden, a 14-year-old from Santa Cruz, California, borrowed a small underwater robot to film kelp forests. He wondered if sea urchins explained why some kelp beds are growing back. His videos showed few urchins anywhere, so something else must be helping. Kelp forests are home to many sea animals.

news.headline: Student Space Experiments Land in a Museum
news.body: A science tool that flew to the International Space Station is now on display at the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. It comes from Genes in Space, a program where students design DNA experiments for astronauts to run in orbit. More than 13,000 students have joined in over the past ten years.

fun_fact: Wombat poop is shaped like little cubes! It's the only animal known to make cube-shaped poop. 🟫
